The confidence intervals provided at each horizon illustrate how uncertainty expands as the forecast period lengthens. Several specific risks and events could cause the actual outcomes to fall outside these predicted ranges. Geopolitical instability, a major regulatory change impacting the market, or unforeseen negative company-specific news (if applicable to the forecast item) could also trigger a substantial decline. Conversely, a breakthrough innovation, surprisingly strong economic performance, a positive resolution to a major global issue, or a sudden surge in market optimism could propel the value well above the upper bounds. These types of high-impact, low-probability events represent the "unknown unknowns" that are difficult to fully quantify within standard probabilistic models, but could nevertheless exert significant influence.
